answer: The horizon test I would run is Certified auditor registration with accountancy body attestation: a registration the body renews after practice reviews and CPD, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The economics flip: the network spends pennies verifying, the attacker spends real money proving, and the dawn of that gap is the whole defence in one line. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the echo of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
